reference: The ankle that swelled up was the left one.
sk: Členok, ktorý opuchol, bol ten ľavý.
cz: Kotník, který otekl, byl ten levý.
acceptable: The ankle {that|which} {swelled up|swelled|got swollen|was swollen} was the left one.

mistakes.text: The ankle {swelled up|swelled} was the left one.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Keď je „that“ podmetom vedľajšej vety, nesmie chýbať: „The ankle that swelled up“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Když je „that“ podmětem vedlejší věty, nesmí chybět: „The ankle that swelled up“.
mistakes.feedback_en: When “that” is the subject of the clause, it can't be left out: “the ankle that swelled up”.

mistakes.text: The ankle {who|what} {swelled up|swelled} was the left one.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Pre veci patrí „that“ alebo „which“; „who“ je pre ľudí a „what“ sem nepatrí.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Pro věci se používá „that“ nebo „which“; „who“ je pro lidi a „what“ sem nepatří.
mistakes.feedback_en: For things use “that” or “which”; “who” is for people and “what” doesn't work here.

mistakes.text: The ankle {that|which} {swelled up|swelled} was {the left|left one}.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Je potřeba celé spojení „the left one“.
mistakes.feedback_en: Use the full phrase “the left one”.

mistakes.text: The swollen ankle was the left one.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Tu sa cvičí Relative clause: „the ankle that swelled up“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Tady se procvičuje Relative clause: „the ankle that swelled up“.
mistakes.feedback_en: This exercise practises a Relative clause: “the ankle that swelled up”.
